ASYNC_DISKPOOL_LOCK.meaning: Threads that create or zero out a file in parallel are coordinating with each other.
causes: file creation or growth
check: enable instant file initialization

ASYNC_IO_COMPLETION.meaning: A task is waiting for asynchronous I/O that is not a data page read, such as backup, restore or file initialization.
causes: a backup or restore in progress
file creation or growth without instant file initialization
check: check for running backups or restores
enable instant file initialization

ASYNC_NETWORK_IO.meaning: SQL Server has results ready and is waiting for the client to take them; usually the application, not the server, is the slow part.
causes: the application handles each row while still reading
very large result sets
slow network between client and server
check: check what the client does while fetching rows
return fewer rows or columns
check network latency to the client

BACKUP.meaning: A task is waiting on backup processing, such as the end of a backup step.
causes: a backup in progress
check: check running backups

BACKUPBUFFER.meaning: A backup task is waiting for a free buffer to hold data.
causes: slow backup device
too few buffers configured
check: check BUFFERCOUNT and MAXTRANSFERSIZE
check throughput of the backup destination

BACKUPIO.meaning: A backup task is waiting on the backup device or for data to send, for example a slow disk or network share.
causes: slow backup destination
network latency to the backup share
check: check throughput of the backup destination

BACKUPTHREAD.meaning: A backup or restore is coordinating its worker threads; long waits simply mirror a long-running backup.
causes: a long-running backup or restore
check: check backup throughput and destination

BACKUP_OPERATOR.meaning: A tape backup or restore is paused until someone mounts the next tape.
causes: tape backups
check: check the tape device

BMPALLOCATION.meaning: A thread of a parallel batch mode plan is waiting to allocate a large bitmap filter.
causes: batch mode hash joins with bitmap filters
check: check MAXDOP and data skew

BMPBUILD.meaning: A thread of a parallel batch mode plan is waiting for a large bitmap filter to be built.
causes: batch mode hash joins with bitmap filters
check: check MAXDOP and data skew

BMPREPARTITION.meaning: A thread of a parallel batch mode plan is waiting for a large bitmap filter to be repartitioned.
causes: batch mode hash joins with bitmap filters
check: check MAXDOP and data skew

BPSORT.meaning: A thread of a batch mode sort is waiting on another thread of the same sort.
causes: batch mode sorts, often with columnstore
check: check the plan for large sorts and memory grants

BROKER_CONNECTION_RECEIVE_TASK.meaning: A Service Broker or mirroring endpoint connection is queued to read an incoming message.
causes: Service Broker transport between endpoints
check: check network between Broker endpoints

BROKER_ENDPOINT_STATE_MUTEX.meaning: A task is waiting for access to the state of a Service Broker or mirroring endpoint.
causes: endpoint configuration changes
check: no action unless it persists

BROKER_EVENTHANDLER.meaning: Idle background wait: the Service Broker event handler task is parked until it has something to process; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

BROKER_INIT.meaning: Service Broker start-up work is running for an active database.
causes: database startup with Service Broker enabled
check: no action unless it persists

BROKER_MASTERSTART.meaning: The main Service Broker event handler has not finished starting yet.
causes: instance startup
check: no action unless it persists

BROKER_RECEIVE_WAITFOR.meaning: Idle background wait: a session sits in WAITFOR RECEIVE until a message lands on a Service Broker queue; it can be ignored.
causes: a Service Broker reader polling an empty queue
check: check the queue reader only if messages pile up

BROKER_REGISTERALLENDPOINTS.meaning: A task is waiting for Service Broker endpoints to initialize.
causes: instance startup
check: no action unless it persists

BROKER_SHUTDOWN.meaning: Service Broker is shutting down in a database.
causes: database or instance shutdown
check: no action unless it persists

BROKER_TASK_STOP.meaning: Idle background wait: a Service Broker queue task is idling until it is stopped or handed new work; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

BROKER_TO_FLUSH.meaning: Idle background wait: the Service Broker lazy flusher idles between saving in-memory transmission objects; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

BROKER_TRANSMISSION_WORK.meaning: Service Broker transmission work is waiting for queued messages to be handled.
causes: Service Broker message traffic
check: check Broker queues for backlog

BROKER_TRANSMITTER.meaning: Idle background wait: the Service Broker transmitter has no outgoing messages to send; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

BUFFERPOOL_SCAN.meaning: A task is waiting for a parallel scan of the buffer pool to finish, for example after dropping or restoring a database.
causes: operations that scan the whole buffer pool on large memory servers
check: expected during such operations; check how often they run

CHECKPOINT_QUEUE.meaning: Idle background wait: the checkpoint task has nothing to do until a new checkpoint is requested; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

CHKPT.meaning: Idle background wait: the checkpoint thread reports that it has started, once at server startup; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

CLRHOST_STATE_ACCESS.meaning: A task is waiting to read or update the CLR host state, usually while the CLR is starting.
causes: first use of CLR after startup
check: no action unless it persists

CLR_AUTO_EVENT.meaning: Idle background wait: a CLR background task is parked on an auto-reset event; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

CLR_CRST.meaning: CLR code is blocked at a critical section that another task is inside.
causes: CLR code contending on shared state
check: review CLR assemblies for shared locks

CLR_JOIN.meaning: CLR code started another task and is blocked until it ends.
causes: CLR code running other threads
check: review the CLR code

CLR_MANUAL_EVENT.meaning: Idle background wait: a CLR background task is parked on a manual-reset event; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

CLR_MEMORY_SPY.meaning: Bookkeeping of CLR virtual memory allocations is serialized behind a lock.
causes: heavy CLR memory use
check: review CLR memory usage

CLR_MONITOR.meaning: CLR code is blocked entering a Monitor (C# lock statement) that another thread holds.
causes: CLR code using Monitor or lock statements
check: review the CLR code

CLR_RWLOCK_READER.meaning: CLR code wants the read side of a reader-writer lock that a writer holds.
causes: CLR code contending on a lock
check: review the CLR code

CLR_RWLOCK_WRITER.meaning: CLR code wants the write side of a reader-writer lock that others hold.
causes: CLR code contending on a lock
check: review the CLR code

CLR_SEMAPHORE.meaning: Idle background wait: a CLR background task is parked on a semaphore; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

CLR_TASK_START.meaning: A newly created CLR task is still starting.
causes: CLR initialization
check: no action unless it persists

CMEMPARTITIONED.meaning: A thread is waiting to allocate from a memory object that is partitioned per node or CPU.
causes: very heavy concurrent memory allocation
check: check compilation rate and memory clerks

CMEMTHREAD.meaning: A thread is waiting to allocate from a memory object that many threads share and that is guarded by a lock.
causes: very high ad hoc compilation filling the plan cache
memory objects not partitioned per CPU on large machines
check: check the compilation rate
check whether the current build or trace flag 8048 helps

CXCONSUMER.meaning: A consumer thread of a parallel query is waiting for producer threads to send rows; mostly harmless on its own.
causes: normal parallel execution
slow producer threads
check: look at CXPACKET and the query's other waits instead

CXPACKET.meaning: A thread of a parallel query is waiting on another thread of the same query to hand over or take rows.
causes: rows spread unevenly across threads (skew)
parallelism used for cheap queries
stale statistics
check: review MAXDOP and cost threshold for parallelism
check per-thread row counts in the actual plan
update statistics on the tables involved

CXROWSET_SYNC.meaning: A thread of a parallel range scan is waiting to synchronize with the other threads of the scan.
causes: parallel range scans
check: review MAXDOP for the query

CXSYNC_CONSUMER.meaning: A consumer thread of a parallel query is waiting at a sync point until all consumer threads have arrived.
causes: parallel plans with uneven work per thread
check: check MAXDOP and data skew in the plan

CXSYNC_PORT.meaning: A thread of a parallel query is waiting to open, sync or close an exchange port with the other threads of that query.
causes: plans with many exchange operators
a slow or skewed parallel branch
check: review MAXDOP for the query
check the plan for skewed parallel branches

DBMIRRORING_CMD.meaning: Idle background wait: a database mirroring task is waiting for log flushes or commands from its partner; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

DBMIRROR_DBM_EVENT.meaning: Idle background wait: a database mirroring task is waiting for a mirroring event; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

causes: heavy mirroring traffic
check: check mirroring send queue

DBMIRROR_EVENTS_QUEUE.meaning: Idle background wait: database mirroring has no queued events to handle; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

DBMIRROR_SEND.meaning: Database mirroring is waiting for the network buffer to have room to send messages.
causes: slow network to the mirror
check: check network throughput to the mirror

DBMIRROR_WORKER_QUEUE.meaning: Idle background wait: a database mirroring worker is waiting for its next job; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

DEADLOCK_ENUM_MUTEX.meaning: Deadlock searches are serialized so the deadlock monitor and waiting-task DMV queries never run one at the same time.
causes: deadlock searches
check: check how often deadlocks occur

DEADLOCK_TASK_SEARCH.meaning: The deadlock monitor and queries on sys.dm_os_waiting_tasks take turns; long waits mean such queries are holding up deadlock searches.
causes: frequent monitoring queries on waiting tasks
check: reduce how often monitoring tools poll waiting tasks

DIRTY_PAGE_POLL.meaning: Idle background wait: the indirect checkpoint background writer polls for dirty pages to write; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

DISABLE_VERSIONING.meaning: A task is waiting for snapshot transactions to finish before row versioning can be turned off.
causes: ALTER DATABASE disabling snapshot isolation
check: find long snapshot transactions

DISKIO_SUSPEND.meaning: A task is waiting because I/O for the database is suspended, usually by a snapshot backup.
causes: VSS or snapshot backups freezing I/O
check: check snapshot backup timing and duration

DISPATCHER_QUEUE_SEMAPHORE.meaning: Idle background wait: a thread in a dispatcher pool has run out of queued work; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

DTC.meaning: A session is waiting on the Microsoft Distributed Transaction Coordinator during a distributed transaction.
causes: distributed transactions across linked servers
a slow or unreachable remote participant
check: check the DTC service and the remote participants

DTC_ABORT_REQUEST.meaning: A DTC worker session is queued to take ownership of a distributed transaction so it can abort it.
causes: distributed transaction rollbacks
check: check the DTC service and remote participants

DTC_RESOLVE.meaning: A recovery task is waiting on master to learn the outcome of a cross-database transaction.
causes: cross-database transactions in doubt at recovery
check: check recovery progress in the error log

DTC_STATE.meaning: A task is waiting for a change to the internal state of a distributed transaction.
causes: distributed transactions
check: check the DTC service

DTC_WAITFOR_OUTCOME.meaning: Recovery found prepared distributed transactions and cannot finish until DTC is reachable to give their outcome.
causes: DTC unavailable at startup
check: check that the DTC service is running

ENABLE_VERSIONING.meaning: A task is waiting for open transactions to finish before row versioning can be turned on.
causes: ALTER DATABASE enabling snapshot isolation
check: find long open transactions

EXCHANGE.meaning: A thread of a parallel query is synchronizing at an exchange operator (an older name for parallel exchange waits).
causes: parallel plans
check: review MAXDOP and cost threshold for parallelism

EXECSYNC.meaning: Idle background wait: parallel threads coordinate on shared helpers such as bitmaps, spools or LOB handling outside the exchange operators; it can be ignored.
causes: parallel plans with bitmaps or spools
check: look at CXPACKET and the query plan instead if parallel queries are slow

EXECUTION_PIPE_EVENT_INTERNAL.meaning: Producer and consumer parts of a batch submitted through a connection are synchronizing.
causes: batch execution plumbing
check: only investigate if it is a top wait

EXTERNAL_SCRIPT_NETWORK_IO.meaning: A session is waiting on network I/O with an external script runtime (R, Python, Java).
causes: sp_execute_external_script running
check: check the external runtime and data volume

FCB_REPLICA_READ.meaning: Reads from the sparse file of a database snapshot, including the hidden one DBCC CHECKDB makes, are being serialized.
causes: DBCC CHECKDB or database snapshots
check: check storage latency during DBCC

FCB_REPLICA_WRITE.meaning: Writes into the sparse file of a database snapshot, including the hidden one DBCC CHECKDB makes, are being serialized.
causes: DBCC CHECKDB or database snapshots
check: check storage latency during DBCC

FSAGENT.meaning: Idle background wait: FILESTREAM file I/O is coordinating through the FILESTREAM agent; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

FT_COMPROWSET_RWLOCK.meaning: A full-text task is waiting on a reader-writer lock for a full-text fragment.
causes: full-text queries during population
check: check full-text population

FT_IFTSHC_MUTEX.meaning: Idle background wait: the full-text host controller holds its internal mutex during background housekeeping; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

FT_IFTS_RWLOCK.meaning: A full-text background task is waiting on a reader-writer lock for full-text metadata.
causes: full-text population or merges
check: check full-text crawl activity

FT_IFTS_SCHEDULER.meaning: A full-text scheduler task is waiting on its internal synchronization.
causes: full-text population
check: check full-text crawl activity

FT_IFTS_SCHEDULER_IDLE_WAIT.meaning: Idle background wait: the full-text scheduler sleeps while no full-text work is queued; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

FT_MASTER_MERGE.meaning: A full-text master merge is running.
causes: full-text catalog reorganization
check: schedule merges in quiet periods

FT_METADATA_MUTEX.meaning: A task is waiting on the mutex that protects full-text catalog metadata.
causes: concurrent full-text DDL or population
check: check full-text maintenance jobs

FT_PROPERTYLIST_CACHE.meaning: A task is waiting on the full-text property list cache.
causes: full-text property searches
check: no action unless it persists

FT_RESTART_CRAWL.meaning: A full-text population hit a transient error and is resuming from its last saved position.
causes: transient full-text failures
check: check the full-text crawl log

FULLTEXT GATHERER.meaning: A task is synchronizing with the full-text gatherer during population.
causes: full-text population
check: check full-text crawl activity

HADR_AG_MUTEX.meaning: An availability group DDL or failover is waiting for exclusive access to the group's configuration.
causes: concurrent availability group DDL or failover
check: check for long-running availability group operations

HADR_AR_CRITICAL_SECTION_ENTRY.meaning: A task is waiting to enter the critical section that protects the availability replica's runtime state.
causes: concurrent availability group DDL or state changes
check: check for long-running availability group operations

HADR_CLUSAPI_CALL.meaning: Idle background wait: an availability group worker is inside a Windows cluster API call; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

HADR_DATABASE_FLOW_CONTROL.meaning: Log sending for a database in an availability group paused because too many messages are waiting for the secondary.
causes: slow or overloaded secondary
network congestion
check: check the secondary's redo and network throughput

HADR_DATABASE_WAIT_FOR_TRANSITION_TO_VER.meaning: A query on a readable secondary is waiting for row versioning to be enabled after a role change.
causes: readable secondary just started or failed over
long transactions on the primary
check: check for long open transactions on the primary

HADR_DBSEEDING.meaning: A task is waiting on automatic seeding of a database to a secondary replica.
causes: automatic seeding in progress
check: check seeding progress in the seeding DMVs

HADR_DB_COMMAND.meaning: An availability group task is waiting for a response to a database-level command sent between replicas.
causes: replica communication delays
check: check network and replica health

HADR_FILESTREAM_IOMGR.meaning: An availability group FILESTREAM transport task is waiting on its I/O manager lock.
causes: FILESTREAM data sent between replicas
check: only investigate if it is a top wait

HADR_FILESTREAM_IOMGR_IOCOMPLETION.meaning: Idle background wait: the FILESTREAM transport of an availability group polls for finished I/O; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

HADR_GROUP_COMMIT.meaning: A commit is waiting so the availability group can send several commits to the secondary together.
causes: group commit batching of synchronous commits
check: usually small; check HADR_SYNC_COMMIT if commits are slow

HADR_LOGCAPTURE_SYNC.meaning: Availability group log capture or apply is synchronizing access to its scan state.
causes: replica state changes or heavy log scanning
check: check replica health

HADR_LOGCAPTURE_WAIT.meaning: Idle background wait: availability group log capture is waiting for new log records to ship; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

HADR_NOTIFICATION_DEQUEUE.meaning: Idle background wait: the task that handles failover cluster notifications has none queued; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

HADR_PARTNER_SYNC.meaning: A task is waiting on the lock that protects the list of availability group partners.
causes: replica configuration changes
check: only investigate if it is a top wait

HADR_RECOVERY_WAIT_FOR_UNDO.meaning: Recovery on a secondary is waiting for undo to finish before it can resynchronize.
causes: failover or resynchronization after a role change
check: check recovery progress on the secondary

HADR_SYNCHRONIZING_THROTTLE.meaning: The primary is slowing log generation so that a synchronizing secondary can catch up.
causes: a secondary that fell behind
heavy log generation
check: check synchronization state and queue sizes of the secondary

HADR_SYNC_COMMIT.meaning: A commit on the primary is waiting for a synchronous availability group secondary to harden its log records.
causes: network latency to the secondary
slow log storage on the secondary
a backlog in the secondary's queues
check: check round trip time and the log send queue
check log write latency on the secondary
use asynchronous commit for distant replicas

HADR_THROTTLE_LOG_RATE_GOVERNOR.meaning: Log generation is throttled because of availability group or service tier log rate limits.
causes: secondaries falling behind
log-heavy work
check: check replica lag and log rate limits

HADR_TIMER_TASK.meaning: Idle background wait: an availability group timer task is waiting for its next scheduled run; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

HADR_TRANSPORT_FLOW_CONTROL.meaning: The availability group transport paused because too many messages are unacknowledged by the replica.
causes: slow network or replica
check: check network latency and throughput between replicas

HADR_TRANSPORT_SESSION.meaning: An availability group task is waiting for the transport session state to change.
causes: replica connection being set up or lost
check: check connectivity between replicas

HADR_WORK_POOL.meaning: Availability group background workers are contending on the work pool's internal lock.
causes: many availability group databases or tasks
check: only investigate if it is a top wait

HADR_WORK_QUEUE.meaning: Idle background wait: an availability group background thread has no work assigned; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

HTBUILD.meaning: A thread of a batch mode hash join or aggregate is waiting for the shared hash table to be built.
causes: batch mode hash operators
skew between threads
check: check memory grant and skew in the plan

HTDELETE.meaning: A thread of a batch mode hash operator is waiting at the end of the operator while the hash table is cleaned up.
causes: batch mode hash operators
check: check skew between threads in the plan

HTMEMO.meaning: A thread of a batch mode hash operator is waiting before scanning the hash table to output matches.
causes: batch mode hash operators
check: check skew between threads in the plan

HTREINIT.meaning: A thread of a batch mode hash operator is waiting before the hash table is reset for the next partial join.
causes: batch mode hash operators that spill
check: check the memory grant for spills

HTREPARTITION.meaning: A thread of a batch mode hash operator is waiting while the hash table is repartitioned.
causes: batch mode hash operators with skew or spills
check: check the memory grant and skew

INSTANCE_LOG_RATE_GOVERNOR.meaning: Log generation is throttled to an instance-level log rate limit, as on Azure SQL Managed Instance.
causes: log-heavy work across databases
check: compare log rate with the instance limit

IO_AUDIT_MUTEX.meaning: Trace and audit event buffers are being handed over under a mutex.
causes: busy traces or audits
check: check running traces and audits

IO_COMPLETION.meaning: A task is waiting for I/O that is not a normal data page read, such as sort or hash spills, log reads or bulk work.
causes: sort and hash spills to tempdb
slow storage
check: look for spill warnings in plans
check tempdb and data file latency

IO_QUEUE_LIMIT.meaning: The number of outstanding I/Os reached a limit, as with Azure SQL file I/O caps.
causes: I/O above the tier or file limit
check: check I/O against the service limits

IO_RETRY.meaning: The OS rejected a disk read or write for lack of resources, so the engine is trying it again.
causes: storage driver or OS resource shortage
check: check the error log and storage health

KSOURCE_WAKEUP.meaning: Idle background wait: the task that talks to the Windows Service Control Manager has no request to handle; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

LATCH_DT.meaning: A thread needs a destroy latch on an internal structure that is not a data page.
causes: internal structures being torn down
check: check sys.dm_os_latch_stats for the latch class

LATCH_EX.meaning: A thread needs an exclusive latch on an internal structure that is not a data page, such as a cache or allocation object.
causes: parallel query contention on shared structures
allocation and file growth structures
metadata or log structures under heavy load
check: check sys.dm_os_latch_stats for the latch class that dominates
check for frequent autogrowth

LATCH_KP.meaning: A thread needs a keep latch on an internal structure that is not a data page.
causes: contention on internal engine structures
check: check sys.dm_os_latch_stats for the latch class

LATCH_NL.meaning: A null-mode latch wait on an internal structure; rarely significant.
causes: internal engine use
check: no action unless it accumulates

LATCH_SH.meaning: A thread needs a shared latch on an internal structure that is not a data page, and another thread holds it exclusively.
causes: contention on internal caches or allocation structures
parallel scans on the same objects
check: check sys.dm_os_latch_stats for the latch class that dominates

LATCH_UP.meaning: A thread needs an update latch on an internal structure that is not a data page.
causes: contention on internal engine structures
check: check sys.dm_os_latch_stats for the latch class

LAZYWRITER_SLEEP.meaning: Idle background wait: the lazy writer sleeps between sweeps of the buffer pool; it can be ignored.
causes: normal background activity of the engine
check: no action needed; leave it out of wait analysis

LCK_M_BU.meaning: A bulk load asked for a table lock and is waiting for the bulk update lock because the table is in use.
causes: BULK INSERT or bcp with TABLOCK while others use the table
parallel bulk loads into a table that has indexes
check: check which load or query holds the table
parallel BU locks only work on heaps without indexes

LCK_M_BU_ABORT_BLOCKERS.meaning: A low priority request for a bulk update (BU) lock with ABORT_AFTER_WAIT = BLOCKERS, so blocking sessions are killed when MAX_DURATION runs out.
causes: ONLINE index operation or partition switch configured to abort blockers
check: expect blocking sessions to be rolled back after MAX_DURATION
schedule the DDL for a quieter window

LCK_M_BU_LOW_PRIORITY.meaning: A low priority request for a bulk update (BU) lock, made by an online index rebuild or partition switch that uses WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY.
causes: ONLINE index rebuild or SWITCH PARTITION with WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY
long-running transactions holding locks on the table
check: find the blocker in the blocking tree
review MAX_DURATION and ABORT_AFTER_WAIT of the DDL

LCK_M_IS.meaning: A session needs an intent shared lock on a table or page, typically blocked by an exclusive lock held at that level.
causes: an escalated table-level exclusive lock
TABLOCKX hints or schema changes on the table
check: look for an escalated table lock in the blocking tree
check for large batch modifications on the same table

LCK_M_IS_ABORT_BLOCKERS.meaning: A low priority request for an intent shared (IS) lock with ABORT_AFTER_WAIT = BLOCKERS, so blocking sessions are killed when MAX_DURATION runs out.
causes: ONLINE index operation or partition switch configured to abort blockers
check: expect blocking sessions to be rolled back after MAX_DURATION
schedule the DDL for a quieter window

LCK_M_IS_LOW_PRIORITY.meaning: A low priority request for an intent shared (IS) lock, made by an online index rebuild or partition switch that uses WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY.
causes: ONLINE index rebuild or SWITCH PARTITION with WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY
long-running transactions holding locks on the table
check: find the blocker in the blocking tree
review MAX_DURATION and ABORT_AFTER_WAIT of the DDL

LCK_M_IU.meaning: A session needs an intent update lock on a page or table, but another session holds an incompatible lock at that level.
causes: page or table level exclusive locks held by another session
check: find the head blocker and the object it holds

LCK_M_IU_ABORT_BLOCKERS.meaning: A low priority request for an intent update (IU) lock with ABORT_AFTER_WAIT = BLOCKERS, so blocking sessions are killed when MAX_DURATION runs out.
causes: ONLINE index operation or partition switch configured to abort blockers
check: expect blocking sessions to be rolled back after MAX_DURATION
schedule the DDL for a quieter window

LCK_M_IU_LOW_PRIORITY.meaning: A low priority request for an intent update (IU) lock, made by an online index rebuild or partition switch that uses WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY.
causes: ONLINE index rebuild or SWITCH PARTITION with WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY
long-running transactions holding locks on the table
check: find the blocker in the blocking tree
review MAX_DURATION and ABORT_AFTER_WAIT of the DDL

LCK_M_IX.meaning: A writer needs an intent exclusive lock on a table or page, typically blocked by a shared or exclusive lock at that level.
causes: a table-level shared lock from TABLOCK, HOLDLOCK or escalation
a table-level exclusive lock from escalation
check: check for lock escalation on the table
look for TABLOCK or HOLDLOCK hints in the blocker

LCK_M_IX_ABORT_BLOCKERS.meaning: A low priority request for an intent exclusive (IX) lock with ABORT_AFTER_WAIT = BLOCKERS, so blocking sessions are killed when MAX_DURATION runs out.
causes: ONLINE index operation or partition switch configured to abort blockers
check: expect blocking sessions to be rolled back after MAX_DURATION
schedule the DDL for a quieter window

LCK_M_IX_LOW_PRIORITY.meaning: A low priority request for an intent exclusive (IX) lock, made by an online index rebuild or partition switch that uses WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY.
causes: ONLINE index rebuild or SWITCH PARTITION with WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY
long-running transactions holding locks on the table
check: find the blocker in the blocking tree

check: usually brief

IPC:ProcSignalBarrier.meaning: The backend is waiting for all other backends to process a barrier event.

IPC:ProcarrayGroupUpdate.meaning: At commit, this backend joined a batch and is blocked until the batch leader removes all their transaction IDs from the process array.

IPC:RecoveryEndCommand.meaning: At the end of recovery the server runs recovery_end_command and is blocked until it returns.

IPC:RecoveryPause.meaning: Recovery is paused and waiting to be resumed.

IPC:ReplicationSlotDrop.meaning: Dropping a replication slot is blocked because a consumer is still attached to it.

IPC:SyncRep.meaning: A commit is waiting for confirmation from a synchronous standby.
